pico.population: Adult patients (>=18 years) with confirmed or suspected splenic lesions or haematological malignancies (including lymphoma, leukaemia, and metastatic disease involving the spleen) undergoing contrast-enhanced CT, MRI, or PET-CT imaging in oncology or radiology departments.
pico.intervention: Radiomics feature extraction from splenic medical images — including first-order statistical features (intensity histogram, entropy, kurtosis), texture features (GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, GLDM), shape and morphological descriptors, and wavelet-transformed features — combined with machine learning or deep learning classifiers (e.g., SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, CNN) to detect, characterise, and classify cancerous splenic involvement.
pico.comparison: Conventional radiological assessment by radiologists using visual inspection and qualitative criteria, standard clinical biomarkers (LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, CBC), histopathological biopsy as the gold standard, and single-feature or non-radiomic imaging approaches.
pico.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of radiomics models for detecting malignant splenic lesions — measured by AUC-ROC, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value; ability to differentiate benign vs. malignant splenic pathology; feature importance rankings identifying the most discriminative radiomic signatures; and model generalisation across imaging protocols and patient cohorts.
pico.hypothesis: Radiomics features extracted from routine CT or MRI images of the spleen can accurately detect and classify cancerous splenic involvement — including primary splenic malignancies and secondary metastatic disease — with diagnostic performance comparable to or exceeding conventional radiological assessment, thereby offering a non-invasive, reproducible biomarker for splenic cancer detection.

key_findings: Radiomics features extracted from spleen CT can achieve excellent diagnostic accuracy for lymphoma vs benign splenomegaly differentiation with 97% accuracy [R5]
First-order statistics and texture features provide highest discriminative power for splenic lymphoma classification based on Random Forest feature importance [R5]
Spleen radiomics can differentiate lymphoma subtypes including HL, DLBCL, MCL, and FL using extensive feature extraction [R6]
Deep learning-based spleen segmentation combined with classification achieves automated splenomegaly etiology differentiation [R1]
Spleen radiomics serves as systemic immunity biomarker with prognostic value across multiple cancer types [R3, R4, R9]
consensus_points: Portal venous phase CT is the optimal imaging protocol for splenic radiomics based on multiple studies [R1, R5, R6]
Random Forest classifiers consistently demonstrate superior performance for splenic radiomics applications [R5, R6]
First-order statistics and GLCM texture features are consistently among the most discriminative feature categories [R5]
AUC-ROC remains the primary evaluation metric across all splenic radiomics studies
contested_areas: Optimal feature selection method remains debated between LASSO and mRMR approaches with limited direct comparison evidence
Superiority of conventional radiomics versus deep learning radiomics requires further investigation with head-to-head comparisons
Optimal segmentation strategy (manual vs automated) lacks consensus with ICC thresholds varying across studies
research_gaps: Limited external validation of splenic radiomics models across multi-center datasets
Comparative effectiveness analysis against conventional radiological assessment remains sparse
Limited investigation of radiomics for splenic metastases differentiation from benign lesions
Standardisation gaps in IBSI compliance and feature harmonisation protocols
Clinical workflow integration pathways for spleen radiomics are underexplored
recommended_methods: Standardized portal venous phase CT acquisition with 1-2mm slice thickness based on [R5, R6]
Random Forest classifier with comprehensive feature extraction (1317 features) as demonstrated in [R6]
Feature selection combining first-order statistics and texture features based on optimal discriminative performance [R5]
Manual segmentation refinement with expert radiologist annotation for optimal reproducibility
benchmark_datasets: Multi-center CT dataset with 326 patients including lymphoma subtypes [R6]
Single-center CT dataset with 139 patients for lymphoma vs benign differentiation [R5]
The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) lymphoma collections for external validation
key_metrics: ICC for feature reproducibility — threshold used: >0.75 acceptable
imaging_protocols: CT: portal venous phase, 1-2mm slice thickness — cited in [R5, R6]
MRI: T1-weighted post-contrast sequences preferred when available

agent_hints.population_planner: Target lymphoma patients with histopathological confirmation as demonstrated in [R5, R6] with cohort sizes of 139-326 patients. Include multiple lymphoma subtypes (HL, DLBCL, MCL, FL) for comprehensive analysis.
agent_hints.segmentation_agent: Employ manual spleen segmentation with expert radiologist refinement as in [R6] which analyzed 326 patients. Target ICC > 0.90 for reproducibility using ITK-SNAP or 3D Slicer tools.
agent_hints.feature_extraction: Extract 1317 IBSI-compliant features per patient as in [R6], prioritizing first-order statistics (10th percentile, Robust Mean Absolute Deviation) and texture features (Correlation, GLCM, GLRLM) which showed highest discriminative power in [R5].
agent_hints.modeling_agent: Use Random Forest classifier with comprehensive feature set as demonstrated in [R6]. Implement 10-fold cross-validation and feature importance analysis using Gini importance metrics.
agent_hints.validation_agent: Target AUC-ROC performance of 0.89–0.97 as benchmarked in [R5, R6]. Include DeLong test for AUC comparison and report sensitivity (89-95%) and specificity (88-98%) metrics. Plan for external validation using TCIA lymphoma datasets.
agent_hints.reporter_agent: Highlight the excellent diagnostic accuracy (97%) achieved in [R5] and comprehensive lymphoma subtype differentiation capability demonstrated in [R6]. Emphasize clinical workflow integration potential for spleen radiomics in lymphoma diagnosis.
